product_overview: MERMAID provides marine condition monitoring and risk indicators for small-scale fishermen and a vendor demand marketplace to improve trip safety and market coordination. The backend exposes health, zone metadata, current conditions, and 7-day forecasts computed from Open‑Meteo data and a PAGASA-inspired risk engine.
core_goals: Surface near real-time marine conditions and a simple SAFE/CAUTION/UNSAFE risk level to help fishermen decide whether to go to sea
Provide a stable API for listing fishing zones and retrieving current conditions and 7-day forecasts per zone
Support vendor demand listings and admin advisories (manifest outlines higher-level product goals — backend focuses on conditions/forecast APIs)
Minimize upstream latency and re-querying via an in-memory TTL cache while documenting limitations for horizontal scaling
Fail clearly when upstream marine/weather services are unavailable so clients can apply safe fallback behavior

features.name: Health Check
features.description: Lightweight service status endpoint returning service status, version, timestamp, and cache entry count for monitoring and readiness checks.
user_flows: GET /health -> Receive 200 with HealthResponse {status, version, timestamp, cache_entry_count}
GET /health -> Receive 500 with error {message} when internal diagnostics fail or dependency check fails

features.name: Fishing Zones Listing
features.description: Returns static metadata for all supported Philippine fishing zones (hard-coded in the service). Useful for populating client zone pickers and linking to conditions/forecast endpoints.
user_flows: GET /conditions/zones -> Receive 200 with array of FishingZone objects containing id, name, coords, and metadata
GET /conditions/zones -> Receive 500 with error {message} if the service encounters an internal error while loading zone metadata

features.name: Current Marine Conditions
features.description: Authenticated endpoints that fetch real-time marine and weather data from Open‑Meteo, apply the risk engine to compute SAFE/CAUTION/UNSAFE, and return per-zone or aggregated conditions. Uses TTL cache to reduce Open‑Meteo calls; upstream failures map to 503 responses.
user_flows: POST /auth/login with valid credentials -> Receive 200 with JWT token
GET /conditions with Authorization: Bearer <token> -> Receive 200 with AllConditionsResponse containing zones and computed risk levels
GET /conditions with no Authorization header -> Receive 401 Unauthorized
GET /conditions with Authorization: Bearer <token> -> Receive 503 Marine data service unavailable when Open‑Meteo downstream fails or times out
POST /auth/login with valid credentials -> Receive 200 with JWT token
GET /conditions/{zone_id} with Authorization: Bearer <token> and valid zone_id -> Receive 200 with ZoneConditions including wave_height, wind_speed, and risk_level
GET /conditions/{zone_id} with Authorization: Bearer <token> and unknown zone_id -> Receive 404 Zone not found
GET /conditions/{zone_id} with no Authorization header -> Receive 401 Unauthorized
GET /conditions/{zone_id} with Authorization: Bearer <token> -> Receive 503 Marine data service unavailable when Open‑Meteo upstream is unreachable

features.name: Marine Forecast
features.description: Authenticated endpoint to fetch a 7-day hourly forecast from Open‑Meteo, aggregate hourly values into daily summaries, and compute the dominant daily risk level. Responses include both daily summaries and hourly breakdowns; upstream failures return 503.
user_flows: POST /auth/login with valid credentials -> Receive 200 with JWT token
GET /conditions/{zone_id}/forecast with Authorization: Bearer <token> and valid zone_id -> Receive 200 with ZoneForecast containing daily summaries and hourly arrays
GET /conditions/{zone_id}/forecast with no Authorization header -> Receive 401 Unauthorized
GET /conditions/{zone_id}/forecast with Authorization: Bearer <token> and unknown zone_id -> Receive 404 Zone not found
GET /conditions/{zone_id}/forecast with Authorization: Bearer <token> -> Receive 503 Marine data service unavailable when Open‑Meteo returns error or times out

features.name: Risk Engine
features.description: Internal computation module that converts raw wave-height and wind-speed inputs into SAFE/CAUTION/UNSAFE using PAGASA-inspired thresholds. The engine is applied to both current-conditions and forecast aggregation endpoints; failures in upstream data prevent risk calculation and surface as 503 errors to clients.
user_flows: POST /auth/login with valid credentials -> Receive 200 with JWT token
GET /conditions/{zone_id} with Authorization: Bearer <token> -> Receive 200 with ZoneConditions that include computed risk_level (risk engine applied to wave_height and wind_speed)
POST /auth/login with valid credentials -> Receive 200 with JWT token
GET /conditions/{zone_id}/forecast with Authorization: Bearer <token> -> Receive 200 with ZoneForecast where each daily summary contains dominant risk_level computed by the risk engine

GET /conditions/{zone_id} with Authorization: Bearer <token> -> Receive 503 Marine data service unavailable when upstream Open‑Meteo data is missing, preventing the risk engine from computing a valid risk_level

Adding new zones requires a code change and redeployment
